data.gender_notes: Veran is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Veran has its origin in the Hebrew language, and it is derived from the word 'veranah', which means 'light, shining one'. In the Bible, this name is associated with the prophet Jeremiah, whose name also means 'the Lord is exalted'. Jeremiah was a key figure in ancient Israel, known for his unwavering faith and prophecies given by God. The name Veran thus carries symbolism of faith, courage, and wisdom, which were also attributes of Jeremiah.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name reflecting God's light and presence

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Veran total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

historical_references.reference: Veran, a Spanish saint, was the bishop of Bracara (Braga) in Portugal during the late 5th to early 6th century. He is known for his efforts to evangelize the pagan people of the region and is considered a patron saint of Portugal.

Veran, a Roman martyr, was a soldier during the persecution of Diocletian in the late 3rd century. He is said to have refused to sacrifice to pagan gods and was executed, becoming a symbol of Christian faith and martyrdom.
